hymns.title: Come, oh, my soul, in sacred lays
hymns.author: Thomas Blacklock, 1754.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Come, oh, my soul, in sacred lays,
Attempt thy great Creator's praise;
But oh! what tongue can speak his fame?
What mortal verse can reach the theme?

[Verse 2]
Enthroned amidst the radiant spheres,
He glory like a garment wears;
To form a robe of light divine,
Ten thousand suns around him shine.

[Verse 3]
In all our Master's grand designs,
Omnipotence with wisdom shines;
His works, through all this wondrous frame,
Bear the great impress of his name.

[Verse 4]
Raised on Devotion's lofty wing,
Do thou, my soul! his glories sing;
And let his praise employ thy tongue,
Till listening worlds applaud the song.

hymns.title: Oh, render thanks to God above
hymns.author: Tate-Brady.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Oh, render thanks to God above,
The fountain of eternal love;
Whose mercy firm, through ages past,
Hath stood, and shall forever last.

[Verse 2]
Who can his mighty deeds express,
Not only vast--but numberless?
What mortal eloquence can raise
His tribute of immortal praise?

[Verse 3]
Extend to me that favor, Lord,
Thou to thy chosen dost afford;
When thou return'st to set them free.
Let thy salvation visit me.

hymns.title: My God! my King! thy various praise
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My God! my King! thy various praise
Shall fill the remnant of my days;
Thy grace employ my humble tongue,
Till death and glory raise the song.

[Verse 2]
The wings of every hour shall bear
Some thankful tribute to thine ear;
And every setting sun shall see
New works of duty, done for thee.

[Verse 3]
But who can speak thy wondrous deeds?
Thy greatness all our thoughts exceeds;
Vast and unsearchable thy ways--
Vast and immortal be thy praise.

hymns.title: Sweet is the work, my God! my King
hymns.author: Isaac Watts.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Sweet is the work, my God! my King!
To praise thy name, give thanks and sing;
To show thy love by morning light,
And talk of all thy truth at night.

[Verse 2]
Sweet is the day of sacred rest;
No mortal care shall seize my breast;
O may my heart in tune be found,
Like David's harp of solemn sound.

[Verse 3]
My heart shall triumph in the Lord,
And bless his works, and bless his word;
Thy works of grace, how bright they shine!
How deep thy counsels! how divine!

hymns.title: My soul shall praise thee, O my God
hymns.author: O. Heigenbotham.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My soul shall praise thee, O my God
  Through all my mortal days,
And in eternity prolong
  Thy vast, thy boundless praise.

[Verse 2]
In every smiling, happy hour,
  Be this my sweet employ;
Thy praise refines my earthly bliss,
  And heightens all my joy.

[Verse 3]
When anxious grief and gloomy care
  Afflict my throbbing breast,
My tongue shall learn to speak thy praise,
  And lull each pain to rest.

[Verse 4]
Nor shall my tongue alone proclaim
  The honors of my God;
My life, with all its active powers,
  Shall spread thy praise abroad.

[Verse 5]
And when these lips shall cease to move,
  When death shall close these eyes,
My soul shall then to nobler heights
  Of joy and transport rise.

hymns.title: Oh, bless the Lord, my soul
hymns.author: Isaac Watts.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Oh, bless the Lord, my soul!
  Let all within me join,
And aid my tongue to bless his name,
  Whose favors are divine.

[Verse 2]
Oh, bless the Lord, my soul,
  Nor let his mercies lie
Forgotten in unthankfulness,
  And without praises die.

[Verse 3]
'Tis he forgives thy sins--
  'Tis he relieves thy pain--
'Tis he that heals thy sicknesses,
  And gives thee strength again.

[Verse 4]
He crowns thy life with love,
  When ransomed from the grave;
He who redeemed my soul from hell,
  Hath sovereign power to save.

hymns.title: Lift up the Gates of Praise
hymns.author: M. E. Servoss.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Lift up the Gates of Praise,
  That we may enter in,
And o'er salvation's walls proclaim
  That Christ redeems from sin.

Cho.--The stars may praise the hand
        That decks the sky above,
      But man alone can tell the pow'r
        Of Christ's redeeming love.

[Verse 2]
God's works reveal his might,
  His majesty and grace;
But not the tender Father's love
  That saves a dying race.

[Verse 3]
Then let the voice of praise
  To heavenly courts ascend,
Till with the songs the angels sing
  Our hallelujahs blend.

[Verse 4]
To him that hath redeemed
  Our souls from sin's dark maze;
The Hope and Savior of mankind,
  Be everlasting praise.

hymns.title: Praise the Lord, ye heavens! adore him
hymns.author: John Kempthorne, 1810.

hymns.title: Hallelujah! song of gladness
hymns.author: Anon.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Hallelujah! song of gladness;
  Song of everlasting joy;
Hallelujah! song the sweetest
  That can angel hosts employ.

Cho.--Praise ye the Lord! sing Hallelujah!
      Praise ye the Lord! sing Hallelujah!
      Praise ye the Lord! sing Hallelujah!
      Praise ye the Lord!

[Verse 2]
Hallelujah! Church victorious,
  Thou mayst lift this joyful strain;
Hallelujah! songs of triumph,
  Well befit the ransomed train.

[Verse 3]
Hallelujah! let our voices
  Rise to heav'n with full accord;
Hallelujah! ev'ry moment
  Brings us nearer to the Lord.

[Verse 4]
But our earnest supplication,
  Holy God, we raise to thee;
Bring us to thy blissful presence.
  Let us all thy glory see.

hymns.title: O worship the King, all-glorious above
hymns.author: Sir Robert Grant, 1839.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
O worship the King, all-glorious above,
And gratefully sing his wonderful love;
Our Shield and Defender, the Ancient of days,
Pavilioned in splendor and girdled with praise.

[Verse 2]
Thy bountiful care, what tongue can recite?
It breathes in the air, it shines in the light;
It streams from the hills, it descends to the plain,
And sweetly distills in the dew and the rain.

[Verse 3]
Frail children of dust, and feeble as frail,
In thee do we trust, nor find thee to fail;
Thy mercies, how tender! how firm to the end,
Our Maker, Defender, Redeemer, and Friend!

[Verse 4]
Our Father and God, how faithful thy love!
While angels delight to hymn thee above,
The humbler creation, though feeble their lays.
With true adoration shall lisp to thy praise.

hymns.title: How charming is the place
hymns.author: S. Stennett.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How charming is the place
  Where my Redeemer God
Unveils the glories of his face,
  And sheds his love abroad!

[Verse 2]
Here, on the mercy seat,
  With radiant glory crowned,
Our joyful eyes behold him sit,
  And smile on all around.

[Verse 3]
To him their prayers and cries,
  Each contrite soul presents;
And while he hears their humble sighs
  He grants them all their wants.

[Verse 4]
Give me, O Lord, a place
  Within thy blest abode;
Among the children of thy grace,
  The servants of my God.

hymns.title: In thy name, O Lord! assembling
hymns.author: Thomas Kelly, 1809.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
In thy name, O Lord! assembling,
  We, thy people, now draw near;
Teach us to rejoice with trembling;
  Speak, and let thy servants hear--
      Hear with meekness--
  Hear thy word with godly fear.

[Verse 2]
While our days on earth are lengthened,
  May we give them, Lord, to thee;
Cheered by hope, and daily strengthened,
  May we run, nor weary be,
      Till thy glory
  Without clouds in heaven we see.

[Verse 3]
There, in worship, purer, sweeter,
  Thee thy people shall adore;
Tasting of enjoyment greater
  Far than thought conceived before;
       Full enjoyment,
  Full, unmixed, and evermore.

hymns.title: God of our salvation! hear us
hymns.author: Thomas Kelly, 1809.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
God of our salvation! hear us;
  Bless, oh, bless us, ere we go;
When we join the world, be near us,
  Lest we cold and careless grow.
       Savior! keep us;
  Keep us safe from every foe.

[Verse 2]
As our steps are drawing nearer
  To our everlasting home,
May our view of heaven grow clearer,
  Hope more bright of joys to come;
       And, when dying,
  May thy presence cheer the gloom.

hymns.title: How sweet to leave the world awhile
hymns.author: Thomas Kelly, 1809.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How sweet to leave the world awhile,
  And seek the presence of our Lord!
Dear Savior! on thy people smile,
  And come, according to thy word.

[Verse 2]
From busy scenes we now retreat,
  That we may here converse with thee:
Ah! Lord! behold us at thy feet;--
  Let this the gate of heaven be.

[Verse 3]
Chief of ten thousand! now appear,
  That we by faith may see thy face;
Oh! speak, that we thy voice may hear
  And let thy presence fill this place.

hymns.title: Thy presence, gracious God! afford
hymns.author: John Fawcett. 1782.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Thy presence, gracious God! afford:
Prepare us to receive thy word;
Now let thy voice engage our ear,
And faith be mixed with what we hear.

[Verse 2]
Distracting thoughts and cares remove,
And fix our hearts and hopes above;
With food divine may we be fed
And satisfied with living bread.

[Verse 3]
To us thy sacred word apply,
With sovereign power and energy;
And may we, in thy faith and fear,
Reduce to practice what we hear.

[Verse 4]
Father, in us thy Son reveal;
Teach us to know and do thy will;
Thy saving power and love display.
And guide us to the realms of day.

hymns.title: Again our earthly cares we leave
hymns.author: John Newton, 1779, _a._
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Again our earthly cares we leave,
  And in thy courts appear;
Again, with joyful feet, we come
  To meet our Savior here.

[Verse 2]
Within those walls let holy peace.
  And love, and concord dwell;
Here give the troubled conscience ease--
  The wounded spirit heal.

[Verse 3]
The feeling heart, the melting eye.
  The humble mind bestow;
And shine upon us from on high,
  To make our graces grow.

[Verse 4]
May we in faith receive thy word,
  In faith present our prayers;
And in the presence of our Lord,
  Unbosom all our cares.

[Verse 5]
Shew us some token of thy love,
  Our fainting hope to raise;
And pour thy blessing from above,
  That we may render praise.

hymns.title: How did my heart rejoice to hear
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How did my heart rejoice to hear
  My friends devoutly say--
"In Zion let us all appear--
  And keep the solemn day!"

[Verse 2]
I love her gates, I love the road;
  The church, adorned with grace,
Stands like a palace, built for God
  To show his milder face.

[Verse 3]
Up to her courts, with joys unknown,
  The holy tribes repair;
The Son of David holds his throne,
  And sits in judgment there.

[Verse 4]
He hears our praises and complaints;
  And, while his awful voice
Divides the sinners from the saints,
  We tremble and rejoice.

[Verse 5]
Peace be within this sacred place,
  And joy a constant guest!
With holy gifts and heavenly grace
  By her attendants blest!

[Verse 6]
My soul shall pray for Zion still,
  While life or breath remains;
There my best friends, my kindred, dwell,
  There God, my Saviour, reigns.

hymns.title: O day of rest and gladness
hymns.author: Christopher Wordsworth, 1858.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
O day of rest and gladness,
  O day of joy and light!
O balm of care and sadness,
  Most beautiful, most bright!
On thee, the high and lowly,
  Before th' eternal throne,
Sing Holy! Holy! Holy!
  To the great Three in One.

[Verse 2]
On thee, at the creation.
  The light first had its birth;
On thee for our salvation,
  Christ rose from depths of earth.
On thee, our Lord, victorious,
  The Spirit sent from heaven,
And thus on thee, most glorious,
  A triple light was given.

[Verse 3]
New graces ever gaining
  From this our day of rest,
We reach the rest remaining
  To spirits of the blest;
To Holy Ghost be praises,
  To Father and to Son;
The church her voice upraises
  To thee, blest Three in One.

hymns.title: How sweetly breaks the Sabbath dawn
hymns.author: Edwin F. Hatfield, 1840
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How sweetly breaks the Sabbath dawn
  Along the eastern skies!
So, when the night of time hath gone,
  Eternity shall rise.

[Verse 2]
How softly spreads the Sabbath light!
  How soon the gloom hath fled!
So o'er the new created sight
  Celestial bliss is spread.

[Verse 3]
What quiet reigns o'er earth and sea,
  Through all the stilly air!
So calm may we this Sabbath be,
  And free from worldly care.

[Verse 4]
Thus let thy peace, O Lord! pervade
  Our bosoms all our days;
And let each passing hour be made
  A herald of thy praise.

[Verse 5]
This peace of God--how full! how sweet
  It flows from Jesus' breast;
It makes our bliss on earth complete,
  It brings eternal rest.

hymns.title: Safely thro' another week
hymns.author: John Newton, 1779. _a._
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Safely thro' another week,
  God has bro't us on our way;
Let us now a blessing seek,
  Waiting in his courts to-day;
Day of all the week the best,
Emblem of eternal rest.

[Verse 2]
While we seek supplies of grace
  Through the dear Redeemer's name,
Show thy reconciling face;
  Take away our sin and shame;
From our worldly cares set free;
May we rest, this day, in thee.

[Verse 3]
May the gospel's joyful sound
  Conquer sinners, comfort saints,
Make the fruits of grace abound,
  Bring relief from all complaints;
Thus let all our Sabbaths prove,
Till we join the church above.

hymns.title: Welcome, sacred day of rest
hymns.author: William Brown, 1822.

hymns.title: Awake, my soul, and with the sun
hymns.author: Bp. Ken, 1709.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Awake, my soul, and with the sun
Thy daily stage of duty run;
Shake off dull sloth, and joyful rise
To pay thy morning sacrifice.

[Verse 2]
Awake, lift up thyself, my heart,
And with the angels bear thy part,
Who all night long unwearied sing
High praises to th' eternal King.

[Verse 3]
Glory to thee, who safe hast kept,
And hast refreshed me when I slept;
Grant, Lord, when I from death shall wake,
I may of endless life partake.

[Verse 4]
Lord, I my vows to thee renew;
Scatter my sins as morning dew;
Guard my first springs of thought and will,
And with thyself my spirit fill.

hymns.title: Savior, breathe an evening blessing
hymns.author: James Edmeston, 1820.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Savior, breathe an evening blessing,
  E'er repose our spirits seal;
Sin and want we come confessing,
  Thou canst save and thou canst heal.

[Verse 2]
Though destruction walk around us,
  Though the arrows past us fly;
Angel guards from thee surround us,
  We are safe if thou art nigh.

[Verse 3]
Though the night be dark and dreary,
  Darkness cannot hide from thee;
Thou art he who, never weary,
  Watchest where thy people be.

[Verse 4]
Should swift death this night o'ertake us,
  And our couch become our tomb,
May the morn in heaven awake us,
  Clad in bright and deathless bloom.

hymns.title: Softly now the light of day
hymns.author: G.W. Doane, 1824.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Softly now the light of day
Fades upon my sight away;
Free from care, from labor free,
Lord, I would commune with thee.

[Verse 2]
Thou whose all pervading eye
Naught escapes without, within,
Pardon each infirmity,
Open fault, and secret sin.

[Verse 3]
Soon, for me, the light of day
Shall forever pass away;
Then, from sin and sorrow free,
Take me, Lord, to dwell with thee.

[Verse 4]
Thou who, sinless, yet hast known
All of man's infirmity;
Then from thine eternal throne,
Jesus, look with pitying eye.

hymns.title: Fading, still fading, the last beam is shining
hymns.author: Selina Huntingdon
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Fading, still fading, the last beam is shining;
Father in heaven, the day is declining;
Safety and innocence flee with the light,
Temptation and danger walk forth with the night.
From the fall of the shade till the morning bells chime,
Shield us from danger, keep us from crime.

Ref.--Father, have mercy,
      Father, have mercy,
      Father, have mercy, thro' Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

[Verse 2]
Father in heaven, O hear when we call;
Hear, for Christ's sake, who is Savior of all.
Feeble and fainting, we trust in thy might;
In doubting and darkness thy love be our light;
Let us sleep on thy breast while the night taper burns,
Wake in thine arms when morning returns.

hymns.title: Sing them over again to me
hymns.author: P.P. Bliss.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Sing them over again to me,
  Wonderful words of life,
Let me more of their beauty see,
  Wonderful words of life,
    Words of life and beauty,
    Teach me faith and duty.

Cho.--Beautiful words, wonderful words,
        Wonderful words of life,
      Beautiful words, wonderful words,
        Wonderful words of life.

[Verse 2]
Christ the blessed One gives to all
  Wonderful words of life;
Sinner, list to the loving call,
  Wonderful words of life;
    All so freely given,
    Wooing us to heaven.

[Verse 3]
Sweetly echo the gospel call,
  Wonderful words of life;
Offer pardon and peace to all,
  Wonderful words of life;
    Jesus, only Savior,
    Sanctify forever.

hymns.title: Behold! the morning sun
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Behold! the morning sun
  Begins his glorious way;
His beams thro' all the nations run,
  And life and light convey.

[Verse 2]
But, where the gospel comes,
  It spreads diviner light;
It calls dead sinners from the tombs
  And gives the blind their sight.

[Verse 3]
How perfect is thy word!
  And all thy judgments just;
Forever sure thy promise, Lord!
  And men securely trust.

[Verse 4]
My gracious God! how plain
  Are thy directions given!
Oh! may I never read in vain,
  But find the path to heaven.

hymns.title: Lord! I have made thy word my choice
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Lord! I have made thy word my choice,
  My lasting heritage;
There shall my noblest powers rejoice,
  My warmest thoughts engage.

[Verse 2]
I'll read the histories of thy love,
  And keep thy laws in sight,
While through the promises I rove,
  With ever fresh delight.

[Verse 3]
'Tis a broad land of wealth unknown
  Where springs of life arise;
Seeds of immortal bliss are sown,
  And hidden, glory lies.

[Verse 4]
The best relief that mourners have--
  It makes our sorrows blest;
Our fairest hope, beyond the grave,
  And our eternal rest.

hymns.title: Father of mercies, in thy word
hymns.author: Anne Steele, 1760.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Father of mercies, in thy word
  What endless glory shines!
Forever be thy name adored
  For these celestial lines.

[Verse 2]
Here may the wretched sons of want
  Exhaustless riches find--
Riches above what earth can grant,
  And lasting as the mind.

[Verse 3]
Here the fair tree of knowledge grows,
  And yields a free repast;
Sublimer sweets than nature knows
  Invite the longing taste.

[Verse 4]
Here the Redeemer's welcome voice
  Spreads heavenly peace around;
And life and everlasting joys
  Attend the blissful sound.

[Verse 5]
Oh, may these heavenly pages be
  My ever dear delight;
And still new beauties may I see
  And still increasing light.

hymns.title: How shall the young secure their hearts
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How shall the young secure their hearts,
  And guard their lives from sin?
Thy word the choicest rules imparts
  To keep the conscience clean.

[Verse 2]
'Tis like the sun, a heavenly light,
  That guides us all the day;
And, through the dangers of the night,
  A lamp to lead our way.

[Verse 3]
Thy precepts make me truly wise;
  I hate the sinners' road;
I hate my own vain thoughts that rise
  But love thy law, my God!

[Verse 4]
Thy word is everlasting truth;
  How pure is every page!
That holy book shall guide our youth,
  And well support our age.

hymns.title: Begin, my tongue, some heavenly theme
hymns.author: Isaac Watts.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Begin, my tongue, some heavenly theme,
  And speak some boundless thing;
The mighty works or mightier name
  Of our eternal King.

[Verse 2]
Tell of his wondrous faithfulness,
  And sound his power abroad;
Sing the sweet promise of his grace,
  And the performing God.

[Verse 3]
His very word of grace is strong,
  As that which built the skies;
The voice that rolls the stars along,
  Speaks all the promises.

[Verse 4]
Oh, might I hear thy heavenly tongue
  But whisper, "Thou art mine!"
Those gentle words should raise my song
  To notes almost divine.

hymns.title: Great God! how infinite art thou
hymns.author: Isaac Watts.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Great God! how infinite art thou!
  What worthless worms are we!
Let the whole race of creatures bow,
  And pay their praise to thee.

[Verse 2]
Thy throne eternal ages stood,
  Ere seas or stars were made:
Thou art the ever-living God,
  Were all the nations dead.

[Verse 3]
Eternity, with all its years,
  Stands present in thy view;
To thee there's nothing old appears--
  Great God! there's nothing new.

[Verse 4]
Our lives through various scenes are drawn,
  And vexed with trifling cares;
While thine eternal thought moves on
  Thine undisturbed affairs.

[Verse 5]
Great God! how infinite art thou!
  What worthless worms are we!
Let the whole race of creatures bow.
  And pay their praise to thee.

hymns.title: Blest be the Father and his love
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Blest be the Father and his love,
  To whose celestial source we owe
Rivers of endless joy above,
  And rills of comfort here below.

[Verse 2]
Glory to thee, great Son of God!
  From whose dear, wounded body rolls
A precious stream of vital blood--
  Pardon and life for dying souls

[Verse 3]
We give the sacred Spirit praise,
  Who, in our hearts of sin and woe,
Makes living springs of grace arise,
  And into boundless glory flow.

[Verse 4]
Thus, God, the Father, God, the Son,
  And God, the Spirit, we adore;
That sea of life and love unknown,
  Without a bottom or a shore.

hymns.title: O God! our help in ages past
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
O God! our help in ages past,
  Our hope for years to come;
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
  And our eternal home.

[Verse 2]
Under the shadow of thy throne,
  Still may we dwell secure;
Sufficient is thine arm alone,
  And our defense is sure.

[Verse 3]
Before the hills in order stood,
  Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting thou art God,
  To endless years the same.

[Verse 4]
A thousand ages in thy sight
  Are like an evening gone;
Short as the watch that ends the night,
  Before the rising sun.

[Verse 5]
The busy tribes of flesh and blood,
  With all their cares and fears,
Are carried downward by the flood,
  And lost in following years.

hymns.title: My God how wonderful thou art
hymns.author: Frederick Wm. Faber, 1849.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My God how wonderful thou art!
  Thy majesty how bright!
How beautiful thy mercy seat,
  In depths of burning light.

[Verse 2]
How dread are thine eternal years,
  Oh, everlasting Lord!
By prostrate spirits day and night,
  Incessantly adored.

[Verse 3]
Oh, how I fear thee, living God!
  With deepest, tenderest fears,
And worship thee with trembling hope,
  And penitential tears.

[Verse 4]
Yet I may love thee, too, O Lord!
  Almighty as thou art,
For thou hast stooped to ask of me
  The love of this poor heart.

[Verse 5]
No earthly father loves like thee,
  No mother, half so mild,
Bears and forbears as thou hast done
  With me, thy sinful child.

[Verse 6]
Father of Jesus! love's reward!
  What rapture will it be,
Prostrate before thy throne to lie,
  And gaze and gaze on thee.

hymns.title: The Lord descended from above
hymns.author: Thomas Sternhold, d. 1549.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The Lord descended from above,
  And bowed the heavens most high;
And underneath his feet he cast
  The darkness of the sky.

[Verse 2]
On cherub and on cherubim
  Full royally he rode;
And on the wings of mighty winds
  Came flying all abroad.

[Verse 3]
He sat serene upon the floods,
  Their fury to restrain;
And he, as sovereign Lord and King,
  Forevermore shall reign.

hymns.title: Ere mountains reared their forms sublime
hymns.author: Isaac Watts.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Ere mountains reared their forms sublime,
  Or heaven and earth in order stood,
Before the birth of ancient time,
  From everlasting thou art God.

[Verse 2]
A thousand ages in their flight
  With thee are as a fleeting day;
Past, present, future, to thy sight
  At once their various scenes display.

[Verse 3]
But our brief life's a shadowy dream--
  A passing thought, that soon is o'er;
That fades with morning's earliest beam,
  And fills the musing mind no more.

[Verse 4]
To us, O Lord, the wisdom give,
  Each passing moment so to spend,
That we at length with thee may live
  Where life and bliss shall never end.

hymns.title: The Lord is King; child of the dust
hymns.author: Josiah Conder.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The Lord is King; child of the dust!
The Judge of all the earth is just;
Holy and true are all his ways;
Let every creature speak his praise.

[Verse 2]
The Lord is King! lift up thy voice,
Oh, earth! and all ye heavens! rejoice;
From world to world the joy shall ring--
The Lord omnipotent is King.

[Verse 3]
The Lord is King! who then shall dare
Resist his will, distrust his care,
Or murmur at his wise decrees,
Or doubt his royal promises?

[Verse 4]
Oh, when his wisdom can mistake,
His might decay, his love forsake,
Then may his children cease to sing--
The Lord omnipotent is King.

hymns.title: Lord! thy glory fills the heaven
hymns.author: Richard Mant, 1828.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Lord! thy glory fills the heaven;
  Earth is with its fullness stored;
Unto thee be glory given,
  Holy, holy, holy Lord.

[Verse 2]
Heaven is still with glory ringing,
  Earth takes up the angels' cry--
"Holy, holy, holy!" singing,
  "Lord of hosts! the Lord most high!"

[Verse 3]
Ever thus in God's high praises,
  Brethren! let our tongues unite;
Chief the heart when duty raises
  God-ward at his mystic rite.

hymns.title: Hail! holy, holy, holy, Lord
hymns.author: C. Wesley, 1767.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Hail! holy, holy, holy, Lord,
  Whom One in Three we know;
By all thy heavenly host adored,
  By all thy Church below.

[Verse 2]
One undivided Trinity
  With triumph we proclaim;
The universe is full of thee,
  And speaks thy glorious name.

[Verse 3]
Thee, holy Father, we confess;
  Thee, holy Son, adore;
And thee, the Holy Ghost, we bless,
  And worship evermore.

[Verse 4]
Hail! holy, holy, holy Lord,
  Our heavenly song shall be
Supreme, Essential One, adored
  In co-eternal Thee!

hymns.title: Jehovah God! thy gracious power
hymns.author: John Thompson, 1810
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Jehovah God! thy gracious power
  On every hand we see;
Oh, may the blessings of each hour
  Lead all our thoughts to thee.

[Verse 2]
Thy power is in the ocean deeps,
  And reaches to the skies;
Thine eye of mercy never sleeps,
  Thy goodness never dies.

[Verse 3]
In all the varying scenes of time,
  On thee our hopes depend;
In every age, in every clime,
  Our Father and our Friend.

hymns.title: It came upon the midnight clear
hymns.author: E.H. Sears, 1850.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
It came upon the midnight clear,
  That glorious song of old,
From angels bending near the earth,
  To touch their harps of gold;
"Peace to the earth, good-will to men,
  From heaven's all gracious King:"
The earth in solemn stillness lay,
  To hear the angels sing.

[Verse 2]
Still through the cloven skies they come,
  With peaceful wings unfurled;
And still celestial music floats
  O'er all the weary world;
Above its sad and lowly plains
  They bend on heavenly wing,
And ever o'er its Babel sounds,
  The blessed angels sing.

[Verse 3]
O ye, beneath life's crushing load,
  Whose forms are bending low,
Who toil along the climbing way,
  With painful steps and slow;--
Look up! for glad and golden hours
  Come swiftly on the wing;
Oh, rest beside the weary road,
  And hear the angels sing!

[Verse 4]
For lo! the days are hastening on,
  By prophet-bards foretold,
When with the ever-circling years
  Comes round the age of gold!
When peace shall over all the earth
  Its final splendors fling,
And the whole world send back the song
  Which now the angels sing!

hymns.title: While shepherds watched their flocks by night
hymns.author: Nahum Tate, 1696.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
While shepherds watched their flocks by night,
  All seated on the ground,
The angel of the Lord came down,
  And glory shone around.

[Verse 2]
"Fear not," said he,--for mighty dread
  Had seized their troubled mind,--
"Glad tidings of great joy I bring
  To you and all mankind.

[Verse 3]
"To you, in David's town, this day,
  Is born of David's line,
The Savior, who is Christ, the Lord;
  And this shall be the sign:

[Verse 4]
"The heavenly babe you there shall find
  To human view displayed,
All meanly wrapped in swathing bands,
  And in a manger laid."

[Verse 5]
Thus spake the seraph; and forthwith
  Appeared a shining throng
Of angels, praising God, and thus
  Addressed their joyful song:

[Verse 6]
"All glory be to God on high,
  And to the earth be peace:
Good-will henceforth from heaven to men
  Begin and never cease!"

hymns.title: Jesus is God! the glorious bands
hymns.author: Frederick Wm. Faber, 1862.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Jesus is God! the glorious bands
  Of holy angels sing
Songs of adoring praise to him,
  Their Maker and their King.

[Verse 2]
He was true God in Bethlehem's crib,
  On Calvary's cross, true God;
He who, in heaven, eternal reigned,
  In time, on earth abode.

[Verse 3]
Jesus is God! there never was
  A time when he was not;
Boundless, eternal, merciful,
  The Word the Sire begot.

[Verse 4]
Backward our thoughts through ages stretch,
  Onward through endless bliss;
For there are two eternities,
  And both alike are his.

[Verse 5]
Jesus is God! oh, could I now,
  But compass land and sea,
To teach and tell this single truth,
  How happy should I be!

[Verse 6]
Oh, had I but an angel's voice,
  I would proclaim so loud,
Jesus, the Good, the Beautiful,
  Is everlasting God.

hymns.title: Angels rejoiced and sweetly sung
hymns.author: William Hurn, 1813.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Angels rejoiced and sweetly sung
  At our Redeemer's birth;
Mortals! awake: let every tongue
  Proclaim his matchless worth.

[Verse 2]
Glory to God, who dwells on high,
  And sent his only Son
To take a servant's form, and die,
  For evils we had done!

[Verse 3]
Good-will to men; ye fallen race!
  Arise, and shout for joy;
He comes, with rich abounding grace
  To save and not destroy.

[Verse 4]
Lord! send the gracious tidings forth,
  And fill the world with light,
That Jew and Gentile, through the earth,
  May know thy saving might.

hymns.title: What grace, O Lord! and beauty shone
hymns.author: Edward Denny, 1839.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
What grace, O Lord! and beauty shone
  Around thy steps below!
What patient love was seen in all
  Thy life and death of woe!

[Verse 2]
Thy foes might hate, despise, revile,
  Thy friends unfaithful prove;
Unwearied in forgiveness still,
  Thy heart could only love.

[Verse 3]
Oh, give us hearts to love like thee;
  Like thee, O Lord! to grieve
Far more for others' sins, than all
  The wrongs that we receive.

[Verse 4]
One with thyself, may every eye,
  In us, thy brethren, see
That gentleness and grace that springs
  From union, Lord, with thee.

hymns.title: In stature grows the heavenly Child
hymns.author: Anon.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
In stature grows the heavenly Child,
  With death before his eyes;
A Lamb unblemished, meek and mild,
  Prepared for sacrifice.

[Verse 2]
The Son of God his glory hides
  With parents mean and poor;
And he who made the heavens abides
  In dwelling-place obscure.

[Verse 3]
Those mighty hands that stay the sky
  No earthly toil refuse;
And he who set the stars on high
  A humble trade pursues.

[Verse 4]
He before whom the angels stand.
  At whose behest they fly,
Now yields himself to man's command,
  And lays his glory by.

[Verse 5]
The Father's name we loudly raise,
  The Son we all adore,
The Holy Ghost, One God, we praise,
  Both now and evermore.

hymns.title: How beauteous were the marks divine
hymns.author: Arthur Cleveland Coxe, 1838.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How beauteous were the marks divine,
That in thy meekness used to shine;
That lit thy lonely pathway, trod
In wondrous love, O Son of God!

[Verse 2]
Oh, who, like thee, so calm, so bright,
Thou God of God, thou Light of Light!
Oh, who, like thee, did ever go
So patient through a world of woe?

[Verse 3]
Oh, who, like thee, so humbly bore
The scorn, the scoffs of men before?
So meek, forgiving, godlike, high,
So glorious in humility?

[Verse 4]
E'en death, which sets the prisoner free,
Was pang, and scoff, and scorn to thee;
Yet love, through all thy torture glowed,
And mercy with thy life-blood flowed.

[Verse 5]
Oh, in thy light, be mine to go,
Illuming all my way of woe!
And give me ever on the road
To trace thy footsteps, Son of God!

hymns.title: My dear Redeemer and my Lord
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My dear Redeemer and my Lord,
I read my duty in thy Word;
But in thy life the law appears,
Drawn out in living characters.

[Verse 2]
Such was thy truth, and such thy zeal,
Such deference to thy Father's will,
Such love and meekness so divine,
I would transcribe and make them mine.

[Verse 3]
Cold mountains and the midnight air
Witnessed the fervor of thy prayer;
The desert thy temptations knew;
Thy conflict and thy victory too.

[Verse 4]
Be thou my pattern, make me bear
More of thy gracious image here;
Then God, the Judge, shall own my name
Among the followers of the Lamb.

hymns.title: Ride on! ride on in majesty
hymns.author: Henry Hart Milman, 1827.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
Hark! all the tribes Hosanna cry;
O Savior meek, pursue thy road
With palms and scattered garments strowed.

[Verse 2]
Bide on! ride on in majesty!
In lowly pomp ride on to die;
O Christ, thy triumphs now begin
O'er captive death and conquered sin.

[Verse 3]
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
The angel armies of the sky
Look down with sad and wondering eyes
To see the approaching sacrifice.

[Verse 4]
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
The last and fiercest strife is nigh;
The Father on his sapphire throne
Awaits his own anointed Son.

[Verse 5]
Ride on! ride on in majesty!
In lowly pomp, ride on to die;
Bow thy meek head to mortal pain,
Then take, O God, thy power and reign.

hymns.title: Ever would I fain be reading
hymns.author:
Ger., Louisa Hensel, 1829.
     Tr., Catherine Winkworth, 1858
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Ever would I fain be reading,
  In the ancient holy Book,
Of my Savior's gentle pleading,
  Truth in ev'ry word and look.
How to all the sick and tearful
  Help was ever gladly shown;
How he sought the poor and fearful,
  Called them brothers and his own.

[Verse 2]
How no contrite soul e'er sought him,
  And was bidden to depart;
How, with gentle words he taught him,
  Took the death from out his heart.
Still I read the ancient story,--
  And my joy is ever new,--
How for us he left his glory,
  How he still is kind and true.

[Verse 3]
How the flock he gently leadeth,
  Whom his Father gave him here;
How his arms he widely spreadeth,
  To his heart to draw us near.
Let me kneel, my Lord! before thee,
  Let my heart in tears o'erflow,
Melted by thy love adore thee,
  Blessed in thee, mid joy or woe.

hymns.title: In vain in high and holy lays
hymns.author: E.S. Lorenz.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
In vain in high and holy lays
My soul her grateful voice would raise;
For who can sing the worthy praise
Of the wonderful love of Jesus?

Cho.--Wonderful love! wonderful love!
        Wonderful love of Jesus!
      Wonderful love! wonderful love!
        Wonderful love of Jesus!

[Verse 2]
A joy by day, a peace by night,
In storms a calm, in darkness light;
In pain a balm, in weakness might,
Is the wonderful love of Jesus.

[Verse 3]
My hope for pardon when I call,
My trust for lifting when I fall;
In life, in death, my all in all,
Is the wonderful love of Jesus.

hymns.title: From Calvary a cry was heard--
hymns.author: John W. Cunningham, 1820.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
From Calvary a cry was heard--
  A bitter and heart-rending cry;
My Savior! ev'ry mournful word
  Bespoke thy soul's deep agony

[Verse 2]
A horror of great darkness fell
  On thee, thou spotless holy One!
And all the eager hosts of hell
  Conspired to tempt God's only Son.

[Verse 3]
The scourge, the thorns, the deep disgrace,
  These thou could'st bear, nor once repine;
But when Jehovah veiled his face,
  Unutterable pangs were thine.

[Verse 4]
Let the dumb world its silence break;
  Let pealing anthems rend the sky;
Awake, my sluggish soul, awake!
  He died that we might never die.

hymns.title: O sacred head, now wounded
hymns.author: Paul Gerhardt, 1659.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
O sacred head, now wounded!
With grief and shame weighed down,
Now scornfully surrounded
With thorns, thine only crown;
O sacred head, what glory,
What bliss, till now, was thine!
Yet tho' despised and gory,
I joy to call thee mine.

[Verse 2]
What thou, my Lord! hast suffered
Was all for sinners' gain;
Mine, mine was the transgression,
But thine the deadly pain;
Lo! here I fall, my Savior!
'Tis I deserve thy place;
Look on me with thy favor;
Vouchsafe to me thy grace.

[Verse 3]
The joy can ne'er be spoken,
Above all joys beside,
When in thy body broken,
I thus with safety hide;
My Lord of life! desiring
Thy glory now to see,
Beside thy cross expiring,
I'd breathe my soul to thee.

hymns.title: Great God, when I approach thy throne
hymns.author: W.B. Bathurst, d. 1877.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Great God, when I approach thy throne
  And all thy glory see;
This is my stay, and this alone,
  That Jesus died for me.

[Verse 2]
How can a soul condemned to die,
  Escape the just decree?
Helpless and full of sin am I,
  But Jesus died for me.

[Verse 3]
Burdened with sin's oppressive chain,
  Oh, how can I get free?
No peace can all my efforts gain,
  But Jesus died for me.

[Verse 4]
And, Lord, when I behold thy face,
  This must be all my plea;
Save me by thy almighty grace,
  For Jesus died for me.

hymns.title: Oppressed with noon-day's scorching heat
hymns.author: H. Bonar, 1857.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Oppressed with noon-day's scorching heat,
  To yonder cross I flee;
Beneath its shelter take my seat:
  No shade like this for me!

[Verse 2]
Beneath that cross clear waters burst,
  A fountain sparkling free;
And there I quench my desert thirst:
  No spring like this for me!

[Verse 3]
A stranger here, I pitch my tent
  Beneath this spreading tree;
Here shall my pilgrim life be spent:
  No home like this for me!

[Verse 4]
For burdened ones a resting-place
  Beside that cross I see;
Here I cast off my weariness:
  No rest like this for me!

hymns.title: Our sins on Christ were laid
hymns.author: J. Fawcett, 1760.

hymns.title: Did Christ o'er sinners weep
hymns.author: Benjamin Beddome, 1787.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Did Christ o'er sinners weep,
  And shall our cheeks be dry?
Let floods of penitential grief
  Burst forth from every eye.

[Verse 2]
The Son of God in tears--
  The wondering angels see!
Be thou astonished, O my soul!
  He shed those tears for thee.

[Verse 3]
He wept--that we might weep--
  Each sin demands a tear;
In heaven alone no sin is found,
  And there's no weeping there.

hymns.title: By thy birth, and by thy tears
hymns.author: Sir Robert Grant, 1815.

hymns.title: Sweet the moments, rich in blessing
hymns.author:
James Allen, 1761.
     Altered by Walter Shirley, 1176.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Sweet the moments, rich in blessing,
  Which before the cross I spend,
Life, and health, and peace possessing,
  From the sinner's dying Friend!

[Verse 2]
Here I'll sit, forever viewing
  Mercy's streams in streams of blood:
Precious drops, my soul bedewing,
  Plead, and claim my peace, with God.

[Verse 3]
Truly blessed is this station,
  Low before the cross to lie,
While I see divine compassion
  Floating in his languid eye.

[Verse 4]
Here it is I find my heaven,
  While upon the Lamb I gaze;
Love I much?--I've much forgiven,--
  I'm a miracle of grace.

[Verse 5]
Love and grief my heart dividing,
  With my tears his feet I'll bathe;
Constant still in faith abiding,--
  Life deriving from his death.

hymns.title: I gave my life for thee
hymns.author: Frances R. Havergal.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I gave my life for thee,
My precious blood I shed,
That thou mightst ransomed be,
And quickened from the dead;
I gave, I gave my life for thee,
What hast thou given for me?

[Verse 2]
My Father's house of light,
My glory-circled throne,
I left for earthly night,
For wand'rings sad and lone;
I left, I left it all for thee,
Hast thou left aught for me?

[Verse 3]
I suffered much for thee,
More than thy tongue can tell,
Of bitterest agony,
To rescue thee from hell;
I've borne, I've borne it all for thee,
What hast thou borne for me?

[Verse 4]
And I have brought to thee,
Down from my home above,
Salvation full and free,
My pardon and my love;
I bring, I bring rich gifts to thee,
What hast thou brought to me?

hymns.title: Deep in our hearts let us record
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1719.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Deep in our hearts let us record
The deeper sorrows of our Lord;
Behold the rising billows roll,
To overwhelm his holy soul.

[Verse 2]
Yet, gracious God, thy power and love
Have made the curse a blessing prove;
Those dreadful sufferings of thy Son
Atoned for sins that we have done.

[Verse 3]
The pangs of our expiring Lord
The honors of thy law restored;
His sorrows made thy justice known.
And paid for follies not his own.

[Verse 4]
Oh, for his sake our guilt forgive,
And let the mourning sinner live;
The Lord will hear us in his name,
Nor shall our hope be turned to shame.

hymns.title: O love! who gav'st thy life for me
hymns.author: From the German. Author unknown.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
O love! who gav'st thy life for me,
  And won an everlasting good
Through thy sore anguish on the tree,
  I ever think upon thy blood!

[Verse 2]
O Love! who unto death hast grieved
  For this cold heart, unworthy thine,
Whom the cold grave and death received,
  I thank thee for that grief divine.

[Verse 3]
I give thee thanks that thou didst die
  To win eternal life for me,
To bring salvation from on high:
  Oh, draw me up through love to thee!

hymns.title: Hosanna to the Prince of Light
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Hosanna to the Prince of Light,
  Who clothed himself in clay,
Entered the iron gates of death,
  And tore the bars away.

[Verse 2]
Death is no more the king of dread,
  Since our Immanuel rose;
He took the tyrant's sting away,
  And spoiled our hellish foes.

[Verse 3]
See how the conqueror mounts aloft
  And to his Father flies,
With scars of honor in his flesh,
  And triumph in his eyes.

[Verse 4]
There our exalted Savior reigns,
  And scatters blessings down;
Our Jesus fills the middle seat
  Of the celestial throne.

hymns.title: Angel! roll the rock away
hymns.author: Thomas Scott, 1772.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Angel! roll the rock away;
Death! yield up thy mighty prey;
See! he rises from the tomb,
Glowing with immortal bloom.

[Verse 2]
'Tis the Savior; angels! raise
Fame's eternal trump of praise:
Let the world's remotest bound
Hear the joy-inspiring sound.

[Verse 3]
Shout! ye saints! in rapturous song,
Let the strains be sweet and strong;
Shout the Son of God, this morn
From his sepulcher new-born.

[Verse 4]
Heaven displays her portals wide;
Glorious Hero! through them ride!
King of glory! mount the throne--
Thy great Father's and thine own.

hymns.title: Now for a tune of lofty praise
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Now for a tune of lofty praise
To great Jehovah's equal Son;
Awake, my voice, in heavenly lays,
And tell the wonders he hath done.

[Verse 2]
Sing how he left the worlds of light,
And those bright robes he wore above;
How swift and joyful was his flight,
On wings of everlasting love.

[Verse 3]
Among a thousand harps and songs,
Jesus, the God, exalted reigns;
His sacred name fills all their tongues
And echoes through the heavenly plains.

hymns.title: Hail! morning known among the blest
hymns.author: E. Wardlaw, 1814.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Hail! morning known among the blest,
  Morning of hope, and joy, and love,
Of heavenly peace, and holy rest,
  Pledge of the endless rest above.

[Verse 2]
Blest be the Father of our Lord,
  Who from the dead hath brought his Son;
Hope to the lost was then restored,
  And everlasting glory won.

[Verse 3]
Mercy looked down with smiling eye
  When our Immanuel left the dead;
Faith marked his bright ascent on high,
  And hope with gladness raised her head.

hymns.title: Rise, glorious Conqueror, rise
hymns.author: Matthew Bridges, 1848.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Rise, glorious Conqueror, rise,
Into thy native skies,
  Assume thy right;
And where, in many a fold,
The clouds are backward rolled;
Pass thro' these gates of gold,
  And reign in light.

[Verse 2]
Victor o'er death and hell,
Cherubic legions swell
  The radiant strain;
Praises all heav'n inspire;
Each angel sweeps his lyre,
And claps his wings of fire;
  Thou Lamb, once slain.

[Verse 3]
Enter, incarnate God!
No feet but thine have trod
  The serpent down;
Blow the full trumpets, blow!
Wider your portals throw!
Savior, triumphant, go
  And take thy crown.

[Verse 4]
Lion of Judah, hail!
And let thy name prevail
  From age to age;
Lord of the rolling years,
Claim for thine own the spheres,
For thou hast bought with tears
  Thine heritage.

hymns.title: Jesus comes, his conflict over,--
hymns.author: Thomas Kelly, 1804.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Jesus comes, his conflict over,--
  Comes to claim his great reward;
Angels round the Victor hover,
  Crowding to behold their Lord;
Haste, ye saints! your tribute bring,
Crown him, everlasting King.

[Verse 2]
Yonder throne for him erected,
  Now becomes the Victor's seat;
Lo, the man on earth rejected!
  Angels worship at his feet:
Haste, ye saints! your tribute bring,
Crown him, everlasting King.

[Verse 3]
Day and night they cry before him,--
  "Holy, holy, holy, Lord!"
All the powers of heaven adore him,
  All obey his sovereign word;
Haste, ye saints! your tribute bring,
Crown him, everlasting King.

hymns.title: The head, that once was crowned with thorns
hymns.author: Thomas Kelly, 1820.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The head, that once was crowned with thorns,
  Is crowned with glory now;
A royal diadem adorns
  The mighty Victor's brow.

[Verse 2]
The highest place that heaven affords
  Is his--is his by right;
"The King of kings, and Lord of lords,"
  And heaven's eternal Light.

[Verse 3]
The joy of all who dwell above,
  The joy of all below,
To whom he manifests his love,
  And grants his name to know.

[Verse 4]
To them the cross, with all its shame,
  With all its grace, is given;
Their name--an everlasting name;
  Their joy--the joy of heaven.

[Verse 5]
They suffer with their Lord below,
  They reign with him above;
Their profit and their joy--to know
  The mystery of his love.

[Verse 6]
The cross he bore is life and health--
  Though shame and death to him;
His people's hope, his people's wealth,
  Their everlasting theme.

hymns.title: There's a glorious kingdom waiting in the land beyond the sky
hymns.author: D. W. Whittle.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
There's a glorious kingdom waiting in the land beyond the sky,
  Where the saints have been gath'ring year by year,
And the days are swiftly passing that will bring the kingdom nigh,
  For the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

Cho.--Oh, the coming of the kingdom draweth near;
      Oh, the coming of the kingdom draweth near!
      Be thou ready, O my soul, for the trumpet soon may roll,
      And the King in his glory shall appear.

[Verse 2]
'Tis the hope of yonder kingdom, and the glory there prepared,
  And the looking for the Savior to appear,
That delivers us from bondage to the world that once ensnared,
  For the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

[Verse 3]
With the coming of the kingdom we shall see our blessed Lord,
  For the King ere the kingdom must appear;
Hallelujah to his name, who redeemed us by his blood!
  Oh, the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

[Verse 4]
Oh, the world is growing weary, it has waited now so long,
  And the hearts of men are failing them for fear;
Let us tell them of the kingdom, let us cheer them with the song,
  That the coming of the kingdom draweth near.

hymns.title: Our Lord is now rejected
hymns.author: D.W. Whittle
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Our Lord is now rejected,
  And by the world disowned,
By the many still neglected,
  And by the few enthroned,
But soon he'll come in glory,
  The hour is drawing nigh,
  For the crowning day is coming by and by.

Cho.--Oh, the crowning day is coming,
        Is coming by and by,
      When our Lord shall come in "power,"
        And "glory" from on high.
      Oh, the glorious sight will gladden,
        Each waiting, watchful eye,
        In the crowning day that's coming by and by.

[Verse 2]
The heavens shall glow with splendor,
  But brighter far than they
The saints shall shine in glory,
  As Christ shall them array,
The beauty of the Savior,
  Shall dazzle every eye,
  In the crowning day that's coming by and by.

[Verse 3]
Our pain shall then be over,
  We'll sin and sigh no more,
Behind us all of sorrow,
  And nought but joy before,
A joy in our Redeemer,
  As we to him are nigh,
  In the crowning day that's coming by and by.

[Verse 4]
Let all that look for, hasten
  The coming joyful day,
By earnest consecration,
  To walk the narrow way.
By gathering in the lost ones,
  For whom our Lord did die,
  For the crowning day that's coming by and by.

hymns.title: Crown his head with endless blessing
hymns.author: William Goode, 1811.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Crown his head with endless blessing,
Who, in God the Father's name,
With compassions never ceasing,
Comes salvation to proclaim.
Hail, ye saints, who know his favor,
Who within his gates are found;
Hail, ye saints, th' exalted Savior,
Let his courts with praise resound.

[Verse 2]
Lo, Jehovah, we adore thee;
Thee our Savior! thee our God!
From his throne his beams of glory
Shine through all the world abroad.
Jesus, thee our Savior hailing
Thee our God in praise we own;
Highest honors, never failing,
Rise eternal round thy throne.

hymns.title: Come, Holy Ghost! in love
hymns.author: Lat. Robert II. of France, 996. Tr., Ray Palmer, 1858.

hymns.title: Come, Holy Spirit, heavenly Dove
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Come, Holy Spirit, heavenly Dove!
  With all thy quickening powers,--
Kindle a flame of sacred love,
  In these cold hearts of ours.

[Verse 2]
Look--how we grovel here below,
  Fond of these trifling toys!
Our souls, how heavily they go,
  To reach eternal joys.

[Verse 3]
In vain we tune our formal songs,
  In vain we strive to rise;
Hosannas languish on our tongues,
  And our devotion dies.

[Verse 4]
Dear Lord! and shall we ever live,
  At this poor dying rate?
Our love so faint, so cold to thee,
  And thine to us so great?

[Verse 5]
Come, Holy Spirit, heavenly Dove
  With all thy quickening powers;
Come, shed abroad a Savior's love,
  And that shall kindle ours.

hymns.title: Spirit Divine! attend our prayers
hymns.author: Andrew Reed, 1841.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Spirit Divine! attend our prayers,
  And make this house thy home;
Descend with all thy gracious powers,
  Oh, come, great Spirit! come.

[Verse 2]
Come as the light; to us reveal
  Our emptiness and woe;
And lead us in those paths of life
  Where all the righteous go.

[Verse 3]
Come as the fire; and purge our hearts,
  Like sacrificial flame;
Let our whole soul an offering be
  To our Redeemer's name.

[Verse 4]
Come as the dove; and spread thy wings,
  The wings of peaceful love;
And let thy church on earth become
  Blessed as the church above.

[Verse 5]
Come as the wind; with rushing sound
  And pentecostal grace;
That all, of woman born, may see
  The glory of thy face.

hymns.title: Eternal Spirit! by whose power
hymns.author: Wm. Riley Bathurst, 1830.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Eternal Spirit! by whose power
  Are burst the bands of death,
On our cold hearts thy blessings shower,
  And stir them with thy breath.

[Verse 2]
'Tis thine to point the heavenly way,
  Each rising fear control,
And, with a warm, enlivening ray,
  To melt the icy soul.

[Verse 3]
'Tis thine to cheer us when distressed,
  To raise us when we fall;
To calm the doubting, troubled breast,
  And aid when sinners call.

[Verse 4]
'Tis thine to bring God's sacred word,
  And write it on our heart;
There its reviving truths record,
  And there its peace impart.

[Verse 5]
Almighty Spirit! visit thus
  Our hearts, and guide our ways;
Pour down thy quickening grace on us,
  And tune our lips to praise.

hymns.title: Gracious Spirit, love divine
hymns.author: John Stocker, 1776.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Gracious Spirit, love divine,
  Let thy light within me shine;
All my guilty fears remove,
  Fill me full of heaven and love.

[Verse 2]
Speak thy pardoning grace to me,
  Set the burdened sinner free;
Lead me to the Lamb of God,
  Wash me in his precious blood.

[Verse 3]
Life and peace to me impart!
  Seal salvation on my heart;
Breathe thyself into my breast,
  Earnest of immortal rest.

[Verse 4]
Let me never from thee stray,
  Keep me in the narrow way;
Fill my soul with joy divine,
  Keep me, Lord, forever thine.

hymns.title: Come, Holy Spirit, come
hymns.author: Joseph Hart, 1759.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Come, Holy Spirit, come;
  Let thy bright beams arise,
Dispel the sorrow from our minds,
  The darkness from our eyes.

[Verse 2]
Revive our drooping faith,
  Our doubts and fears remove,
And kindle in our breasts the flame
  Of never dying love.

[Verse 3]
'Tis thine to cleanse the heart,
  To sanctify the soul,
To pour fresh life in ev'ry part,
  And new create the whole.

[Verse 4]
Dwell, Spirit, in our hearts;
  Our minds from bondage free.
Then shall we know, and praise, and love,
  The Father, Son, and thee.

hymns.title: Holy Spirit, Fount of blessing
hymns.author: Thomas J. Judkin.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Holy Spirit, Fount of blessing,
  Ever watchful, ever kind,
Thy celestial aid possessing,
  Prisoned souls deliverance find.

[Verse 2]
Seal of truth, and Bond of union,
  Source of light, and Flame of love,
Symbol of divine communion,
  In the olive-bearing dove.

[Verse 3]
Heavenly Guide from paths of error,
  Comforter of minds distressed,
When the billows fill with terror;
  Pointing to an ark of rest.

[Verse 4]
Promised Pledge, eternal Spirit,
  Greater than all gifts below,
May our hearts thy grace inherit;
  May our lips thy glories show!

hymns.title: Ah! how shall fallen man
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Ah! how shall fallen man
  Be just before his God?
If he contend in righteousness,
  We fall beneath his rod.

[Verse 2]
If he our ways should mark
  With strict inquiring eyes,
Could we for one of thousand faults
  A just excuse devise?

[Verse 3]
All-seeing, powerful God,
  Who can with thee contend?
Or who that tries the unequal strife,
  Shall prosper in the end?

[Verse 4]
Ah! how shall guilty man
  Contend with such a God?
None, none can meet him and escape,
  But through the Savior's blood.

hymns.title: How heavy is the night
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How heavy is the night
  That hangs upon our eyes,
Till Christ with his reviving light
  Over our souls arise.

[Verse 2]
Our guilty spirits dread
  To meet the wrath of heaven;
But, in his righteousness arrayed,
  We see our sins forgiven.

[Verse 3]
The powers of hell agree
  To hold our souls in vain;
He sets the sons of bondage free,
  And breaks the cursed chain.

[Verse 4]
Lord, we adore thy ways
  To bring us near to God,
Thy sovereign power, thy healing grace,
  And thine atoning blood.

hymns.title: How sad our state by nature is
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1707.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
How sad our state by nature is!
  Our sin--how deep it stains!
And Satan binds our captive minds,
  Fast in his slavish chains.

[Verse 2]
But there's a voice of sovereign grace
  Sounds from the sacred word;--
"Ho! ye despairing sinners! come
  And trust a faithful Lord."

[Verse 3]
My soul obeys the gracious call
  And runs to this relief;
I would believe thy promise, Lord!
  Oh! help my unbelief.

[Verse 4]
To the blest fountain of thy blood,
  Incarnate God! I fly;
Here let me wash my spotted soul,
  From crimes of deepest dye.

[Verse 5]
A guilty, weak, and helpless worm,
  On thy kind arms I fall;
Be thou my strength and righteousness
  My Jesus, and my all.

hymns.title: Buried in shadows of the night
hymns.author: Isaac Watts, 1709.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Buried in shadows of the night
We lie, till Christ restores the light;
Till he descends to heal the blind,
And chase the darkness of the mind.

[Verse 2]
Our guilty souls are drowned in tears,
Till his atoning blood appears;
Then we awake from deep distress,
And sing the Lord our righteousness.

[Verse 3]
Jesus beholds where Satan reigns,
And binds his slaves in heavy chains;
He sets the prisoners free, and breaks
The iron bondage from our necks.

[Verse 4]
Poor, helpless worms in thee possess
Grace, wisdom, power, and righteousness
Thou art our mighty all, and we
Give our whole selves, O Lord, to thee.

hymns.title: There is a fountain filled with blood
hymns.author: William Cowper, 1779.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
There is a fountain filled with blood,
  Drawn from Immanuel's veins,
And sinners plunged beneath that flood,
  Lose all their guilty stains.

Cho.--Oh, glorious fountain!
        Here will I stay,
      And in thee ever
        Wash my sins away.

[Verse 2]
The dying thief rejoiced to see,
  That fountain in his day,
And there may I, though vile as he,
  Wash all my sins away.

[Verse 3]
Thou dying Lamb, thy precious blood,
  Shall never lose its power,
Till all the ransomed church of God,
  Are saved to sin no more.

[Verse 4]
E'er since by faith I saw the stream
  Thy flowing wounds supply,
Redeeming love has been my theme,
  And shall be till I die.

[Verse 5]
And when this feeble, faltering tongue
  Lies silent in the grave,
Then in a nobler, sweeter song,
  I'll sing thy power to save.

hymns.title: Salvation! oh, the joyful sound
hymns.author: Isaac Watts.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Salvation! oh, the joyful sound!
  What pleasure to our ears;
A sovereign balm for every wound,
  A cordial for our fears.

[Verse 2]
Salvation! let the echo fly
  The spacious earth around,
While all the armies of the sky
  Conspire to raise the sound.

[Verse 3]
Salvation! O thou bleeding Lamb!
  To Thee the praise belongs:
Salvation shall inspire our hearts,
  And dwell upon our tongues.

hymns.title: Not all the blood of beasts
hymns.author: Isaac Watts
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Not all the blood of beasts,
  On Jewish altars slain,
Could give the guilty conscience peace,
  Or wash away the stain.

[Verse 2]
But Christ, the heavenly Lamb,
  Takes all our sins away;
A sacrifice of nobler name,
  And richer blood than they.

[Verse 3]
My faith would lay her hand
  On that dear head of Thine,
While like a penitent I stand,
  And there confess my sin.

[Verse 4]
My soul looks back to see
  The burden thou didst bear;
While hanging on the cursed tree,
  And knows her guilt was there.

hymns.title: Like Noah's weary dove
hymns.author: Wm. A. Muhlenberg.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Like Noah's weary dove
  That soared the earth around,
But not a resting place above
  The cheerless waters found,

[Verse 2]
Oh, cease, my wandering soul,
  On restless wing to roam;
All the wide world, to either pole,
  Has not for thee a home.

[Verse 3]
Behold the ark of God,
  Behold the open door;
Hasten to gain that dear abode,
  And rove, my soul, no more.

[Verse 4]
There safe thou shalt abide,
  There sweet shall be thy rest,
And every longing satisfied,
  With full salvation blessed.

hymns.title: Depth of mercy! can there be
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1740.

hymns.title: Arise, my soul, arise
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Arise, my soul, arise,
  Shake off thy guilty fears;
The bleeding sacrifice
  In my behalf appears;
Before the throne my Surety stands,
My name is written on his hands.

[Verse 2]
He ever lives above,
  For me to intercede;
His all-redeeming love,
  His precious blood to plead;
His blood atoned for all our race,
And sprinkles now the throne of grace.

[Verse 3]
Five bleeding wounds he bears,
  Received on Calvary;
They pour effectual prayers,
  They strongly speak for me;
Forgive him, O forgive, they cry,
Nor let that ransomed sinner die.

[Verse 4]
The Father hears him pray,
  His dear Anointed One;
He cannot turn away
  The presence of his Son;
His Spirit answers to the blood,
And tells me I am born of God.

[Verse 5]
My God is reconciled,
  His pard'ning voice I hear,
He owns me for his child,
  I can no longer fear;
With confidence I now draw nigh,
And Father, Abba, Father, cry.

hymns.title: Come to the blood-stained tree
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Come to the blood-stained tree;
  The Victim bleeding lies;
God sets the sinner free,
  Since Christ, a ransom, dies.

[Verse 2]
The Spirit will apply
  His blood to cleanse thy stain;
Oh, burdened soul, draw nigh,
  For none can come in vain!

[Verse 3]
Dark though thy guilt appear,
  And deep its crimson stain,
There's boundless mercy here,
  Oh, do not still disdain.

[Verse 4]
Look not within for peace,
  Within, there's nought to cheer;
Look up, and find release
  From sin, and self, and fear.

hymns.title: 'Tis grace, 'tis grace, 'tis wonderful grace
hymns.author: Rev. W. H. Burrell.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
'Tis grace, 'tis grace, 'tis wonderful grace,
  This great salvation brings;
The soul, delivered of its load,
  In sweetest rapture sings.

Cho.--'Tis grace, 'tis grace,
      Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful grace,
      'Tis grace, 'tis grace,
      Flowing still freely for me.

[Verse 2]
'Tis grace, 'tis grace, 'tis wonderful grace,
  Which saves the soul from sin,
The power of rising evil days,
  And reigns supreme within.

[Verse 3]
'Tis grace, 'tis grace, 'tis wonderful grace;
  Its streams are full and free;
Are flowing now for all the race,
  They even flow to me.

hymns.title: Behold a stranger at the door
hymns.author: Joseph Grigg, 1765.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Behold a stranger at the door,
He gently knocks, has knocked before;
Has waited long, is waiting still;
You treat no other friend so ill.

Cho.--Oh, let the dear Savior come in,
      He'll cleanse the heart from sin,
      Oh, keep him no more out at the door,
      But let the dear Savior come in.

[Verse 2]
Oh, lovely attitude--he stands
With melting heart and loaded hands;
Oh, matchless kindness--and he shows
This matchless kindness to his foes.

[Verse 3]
But will he prove a friend indeed?
He will--the very friend you need;
The Friend of sinners? Yes, 'tis he.
With garments died on Calvary.

[Verse 4]
Rise, touched with gratitude divine,
Turn out his enemy and thine;
That soul-destroying monster, sin,
And let the heavenly stranger in.

[Verse 5]
Admit him, ere his anger burn--
His feet, departed, ne'er return;
Admit him, or the hour's at hand
You'll at his door rejected stand.

hymns.title: Sinners, turn; why will ye die?
hymns.author: Rev. C. Wesley, 1745.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Sinners, turn; why will ye die?
God, your Maker, asks you why?
God, who did your being give,
Made you with himself to live;
He the fatal cause demands;
Asks the work of his own hands,--
Why, ye thankless creatures, why
Will ye cross his love, and die?

[Verse 2]
Sinners, turn; why will ye die?
God, your Savior, asks you why?
He, who did your souls retrieve,
Died himself, that ye might live.
Will ye let him die in vain?
Crucify your Lord again?
Why, ye ransomed sinners, why
Will ye slight his grace and die?

[Verse 3]
Sinners, turn; why will ye die?
God; the Spirit, asks you why?
He who all your lives hath strove,
Urged you to embrace his love.
Will ye not his grace receive?
Will ye still refuse to live?
O ye dying sinners, why,
Why will ye forever die?

hymns.title: Come, says Jesus' sacred voice
hymns.author: Mrs. Anna L. Barbauld, 1812.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Come, says Jesus' sacred voice,
Come, and make my paths your choice;
I will guide you to your home;
Weary pilgrim! hither come.

[Verse 2]
Thou, who, houseless, sole, forlorn,
Long hast borne the proud world's scorn,
Long hast roamed this barren waste,
Weary pilgrim! hither haste.

[Verse 3]
Ye, who, tossed on beds of pain,
Seek for ease, but seek in vain!
Ye, by fiercer anguish torn,
In remorse for guilt who mourn!--

[Verse 4]
Hither come, for here is found
Balm that flows for every wound,
Peace that ever shall endure,
Rest eternal, sacred, sure.

hymns.title: From the cross uplifted high
hymns.author: T. Haweis, 1792.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
From the cross uplifted high,
Where the Savior deigns to die,
What melodious sounds we hear,
Bursting on the ravished ear!--
"Love's redeeming' work is done--
Come and welcome, sinner, come!

[Verse 2]
"Sprinkled now with blood the throne--
Why beneath thy burdens groan?
On my pierced body laid,
Justice owns the ransom paid--
Bow the knee, and kiss the Son--
Come and welcome, sinner, come!

[Verse 3]
"Spread for thee, the festal board--
See with richest bounty stored;
To thy Father's bosom pressed,
Thou shalt be a child confessed,
Never from his house to roam;
Come and welcome, sinner, come!

[Verse 4]
"Soon the days of life shall end--
Lo, I come--your Savior, Friend!
Safe your spirit to convey
To the realms of endless day,
Up to my eternal home
Come and welcome, sinner, come!"

hymns.title: There is a line by us unseen
hymns.author: Joseph Addison Alexander.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
There is a line by us unseen,
  That crosses every path,
The hidden boundary between
  God's patience and his wrath.

[Verse 2]
To pass that limit is to die,
  To die as if by stealth;
It does not quench the beaming eye,
  Nor pale the glow of health.

[Verse 3]
Oh! where is this mysterious bourne
  By which our path is crossed;
Beyond which God himself hath sworn
  That he who goes is lost?

[Verse 4]
How far may we go on to sin?
  How long will God forbear?
Where does hope end, and where begin
  The confines of despair?

[Verse 5]
An answer from the skies is sent,--
  "Ye that from God depart,
While it is called to-day, repent,
  And harden not your heart."

hymns.title: Say, sinner, hath a voice within
hymns.author: Mrs. Ann B. Hyde.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Say, sinner, hath a voice within
  Oft whispered to thy secret soul,
Urged thee to leave the ways of sin,
  And yield thy heart to God's control?

[Verse 2]
Sinner! it was a heavenly voice,--
  It was the Spirit's gracious call;
It bade thee make the better choice,
  And haste to seek in Christ thine all.

[Verse 3]
Spurn not the call for life and light;
  Regard in time the warning kind;
That call thou may'st not always slight
  And yet the gate of mercy find.

[Verse 4]
God's Spirit will not always strive
  With hardened self-destroying men;
Ye, who persist his love to grieve,
  May never hear his voice again.

[Verse 5]
Sinner! perhaps this very day
  Thy last accepted time may be:
Oh! should'st thou grieve him now away
  Then hope may never beam on thee.

hymns.title: Jesus is tenderly calling thee home--
hymns.author: Fanny J. Crosby.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Jesus is tenderly calling thee home--
  Calling to-day, calling to-day;
Why from the sunshine of love wilt thou roam
  Farther and farther away?

Ref.--Calling to-day,
      Calling to-day.
      Jesus is calling,
      Is tenderly calling to-day.

[Verse 2]
Jesus is calling the weary to rest--
  Calling to-day, calling to-day;
Bring him thy burden and thou shalt be blest;
  He will not turn thee away.

[Verse 3]
Jesus is waiting, oh, come to him now--
  Waiting to-day, waiting to-day;
Come with thy sins, at his feet lowly bow;
  Come, and no longer delay.

[Verse 4]
Jesus is pleading, oh, list to his voice--
  Hear him to-day, hear him to-day;
They who believe on his name shall rejoice;
  Quickly arise and away.

hymns.title: Delay not, delay not; oh, sinner! draw near
hymns.author: Thomas Hastings, 1831.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Delay not, delay not; oh, sinner! draw near;
  The waters of life are now flowing for thee;
No price is demanded, the Savior is here,
  Redemption is purchased, salvation is free.

[Verse 2]
Delay not, delay not; why longer abuse
  The love and compassion of Jesus, thy God?
A fountain is opened,--how canst thou refuse
  To wash, and be cleansed in his pardoning blood?

[Verse 3]
Delay not, delay not, oh, sinner! to come,
  For mercy still lingers and calls thee to-day;
Her voice is not heard in the vale of the tomb,--
  Her message, unheeded, will soon pass away.

[Verse 4]
Delay not, delay not; the Spirit of grace,
  Long grieved and resisted, may take its sad flight;
And leave thee in darkness to finish thy race,--
  To sink in the vale of eternity's night.

hymns.title: Come to Jesus, come to Jesus
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Come to Jesus, come to Jesus,
  Come to Jesus just now,
Just now come to Jesus,
  Come to Jesus just now.

[Verse 2]
He will save you.

[Verse 3]
Oh, believe him.

[Verse 4]
He is able.

[Verse 5]
He is willing.

[Verse 6]
He'll receive you.

[Verse 7]
Call upon him.

[Verse 8]
He will hear you.

[Verse 9]
Look unto him.

[Verse 10]
He'll forgive you.

[Verse 11]
Flee to Jesus.

[Verse 12]
He will cleanse you.

[Verse 13]
He will clothe you.

[Verse 14]
Jesus loves you.

[Verse 15]
Don't reject him.

[Verse 16]
Only trust him.

[Verse 17]
Hallelujah. Amen.

hymns.title: There's a stranger at the door
hymns.author: Rev. J. B. Atchison.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
There's a stranger at the door,
         Let him in,
He has been there oft before,
        Let him in;
Let him in ere he is gone,
Let him in, the Holy One,
Jesus Christ, the Father's Son,
        Let him in.

[Verse 2]
Open now to him your heart,
        Let him in,
If you wait he will depart,
        Let him in;
Let him in, he is your Friend,
He your soul will sure defend,
He will keep you to the end,
        Let him in.

[Verse 3]
Hear you now his loving voice?
        Let him in,
Now, oh, now make him your choice
        Let him in;
He is standing at the door,
Joy to you he will restore,
And his name you will adore,
        Let him in.

[Verse 4]
Now admit the heavenly Guest,
        Let him in,
He will make for you a feast,
        Let him in;
He will speak your sins forgiv'n,
And when earth ties all are riven,
He will take you home to heaven,
        Let him in.

hymns.title: To-day the Savior calls
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
To-day the Savior calls!
  Ye wand'rers, come,
Oh, ye benighted souls,
  Why longer roam?

[Verse 2]
To-day the Savior calls!
  Oh, hear him now;
Within these sacred walls
  To Jesus bow.

[Verse 3]
Today the Savior calls!
  For refuge fly!
The storm of justice falls,
  And death is nigh.

[Verse 4]
The Spirit calls to-day;
  Yield to his power;
Oh, grieve him not away,
  'Tis mercy's hour.

hymns.title: Listen, sinner! mercy hails you
hymns.author: Andrew Reed, 1817.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Listen, sinner! mercy hails you;
  With her sweetest voice she calls;
Bids you hasten to the Savior,
  Ere the hand of justice falls:
        Listen, sinner!
  'Tis the voice of mercy calls.

[Verse 2]
See! the storm of vengeance gathering
  O'er the path you dare to tread!
Hark! the awful thunders rolling
  Loud and louder o'er your head!
        Flee, oh, sinner!
  Lest the lightnings strike you dead.

[Verse 3]
Haste, ah! hasten to the Savior;
  Sue his mercy while you may;
Soon the day of grace is over;
  Soon your life will pass away,
        Hasten sinner!
  You must perish, if you stay.

hymns.title: Soon the evening shadows falling
hymns.author: J. W. Slaughenhaupt.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Soon the evening shadows falling
  Close the day of mortal life;
Soon the hand of death appalling
  Draws thee from its weary strife.

Cho.--Are you ready? are you ready?
        'Tis the Spirit calling, why delay?
      Are you ready? are you ready?
        Do not linger longer, come to-day.

[Verse 2]
Soon the awful trumpet sounding
  Calls thee to the judgment throne;
Now prepare, for love abounding
  Yet has left thee not alone.

[Verse 3]
Oh, how fatal 'tis to linger!
  Art thou ready--ready now?
Ready should Death's icy finger
  Lay its chill upon thy brow?

[Verse 4]
Priceless love and free salvation
  Freely still are offered thee;
Yield no longer to temptation,
  But from sin and sorrow flee.

hymns.title: Oh, where shall rest be found--
hymns.author: James Montgomery, 1819.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Oh, where shall rest be found--
  Rest for the weary soul?
'Twere vain the ocean depths to sound,
  Or pierce to either pole.

[Verse 2]
The world can never give
  The bliss for which we sigh;
'Tis not the whole of life to live,
  Nor all of death to die.

[Verse 3]
Beyond this vale of tears
  There is a life above,
Unmeasured by the flight of years;
  And all that life is love.

[Verse 4]
There is a death, whose pang
  Outlasts the fleeting breath;
Oh, what eternal horrors hang
  Around the second death!

[Verse 5]
Lord God of truth and grace,
  Teach us that death to shun,
Lest we be banished from thy face,
  And evermore undone.

hymns.title: Called to the feast by the King are we
hymns.author: J.E. Landor.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Called to the feast by the King are we,
  Sitting, perhaps, where his people be,
How will it fare, friend, with thee and me,
  When the King comes in?

Ref.--When the King comes in, brother,
        When the King comes in!
      How will it fare with thee and me
        When the King comes in?

[Verse 2]
Crowns on the head where the thorns have been,
  Glorified he who once died for men,
Splendid the vision before us then,
  When the King comes in.

[Verse 3]
Like lightning's flash will that instant show
  Things hidden long from both friend and foe,
Just what we are will each neighbor know,
  When the King comes in.

[Verse 4]
Joyful his eye shall on each one rest
  Who is in white wedding garments dressed,
Ah, well for us if we stand the test,
  When the King comes in.

[Verse 5]
Endless the separation then,
  Bitter the cry of deluded men,
Awful that moment beyond all ken,
  When the King comes in.

[Verse 6]
Lord, grant us all, we implore thee, grace,
  So to await thee each in his place,
That we may fear not to see thy face
  When thou comest in.

hymns.title: Oh, that my load of sin were gone
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1742.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Oh, that my load of sin were gone;
  Oh, that I could at last submit
At Jesus' feet to lay it down--
  To lay my soul at Jesus' feet.

[Verse 2]
Rest for my soul I long to find;
  Savior of all, if mine thou art,
Give me the meek and lowly mind,
  And stamp thine image on my heart.

[Verse 3]
Break off the yoke of inbred sin,
  And fully set my spirit free;
I cannot rest till pure within--
  Till I am wholly lost in thee.

[Verse 4]
Fain would I learn of thee, my God;
  Thy light and easy burden prove;
The cross all stained with hallowed blood,
  The labor of thy dying love.

[Verse 5]
I would, but thou must give the power;
  My heart from every sin release;
Bring near, bring near the joyful hour,
  And fill me with thy perfect peace.

hymns.title: Stay, thou insulted Spirit, stay
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1749.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Stay, thou insulted Spirit, stay,
  Though I have done thee such despite,
Nor cast the sinner quite away,
  Nor take thine everlasting flight.

[Verse 2]
Though I have steeled my stubborn heart,
  And still shook off my guilty fears;
And vexed and urged, thee to depart,
  For many long rebellious years.

[Verse 3]
Though I have most unfaithful been,
  Of all whoe'er thy grace received!
Ten thousand times thy goodness seen;
  Ten thousand times thy goodness grieved;

[Verse 4]
This only woe I deprecate;
  This only plague I pray remove;
Nor leave me in my lost estate;
  Nor curse me with this want of love.

[Verse 5]
Now, Lord, my weary soul release,
  Upraise me with thy gracious hand,
And guide into thy perfect peace,
  And bring me to the promised land.

hymns.title: And can I yet delay
hymns.author: Charles Wesley, 1746.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
And can I yet delay
  My little all to give?
To tear my soul from earth away,
  For Jesus to receive?

[Verse 2]
Nay, but I yield, I yield,
  I can hold out no more:
I sink, by dying love compelled,
  And own thee conqueror.

[Verse 3]
Tho' late, I all forsake,
  My friends, my all resign;
Gracious Redeemer, take, oh, take,
  And seal me ever thine.

[Verse 4]
Come and possess me whole,
  Nor hence again remove;
Settle and fix my wav'ring soul
  With all thy weight of love.

hymns.title: Father, I stretch my hand to thee
hymns.author: Charles Wesley
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Father, I stretch my hand to thee;
  No other help I know:
If thou withdraw thyself from me,
  Ah! whither shall I go?

Cho.--I do believe, I now believe
        That Jesus died for me;
      And thro' his blood, his precious blood,
        I shall from sin be free.

[Verse 2]
What did thine only Son endure.
  Before I drew my breath?
What pain, what labor, to secure
  My soul from endless death!

[Verse 3]
O Jesus, could I this believe,
  I now should feel thy power;
And all my wants thou would'st relieve,
  In this accepted hour.

[Verse 4]
Author of faith! to thee I lift
  My weary, longing eyes;
Oh, let me now receive that gift--
  My soul without it dies.

[Verse 5]
Surely thou canst not let me die;
  Oh, speak, and I shall live,
And here I will unwearied lie,
  Till thou thy Spirit give.

[Verse 6]
How would my fainting soul rejoice,
  Could I but see thy face;
Now let me hear thy quick'ning voice,
  And taste thy pard'ning grace.

hymns.title: Approach, my soul, the mercy-seat
hymns.author: John Newton, 1779.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Approach, my soul, the mercy-seat,
  Where Jesus answers prayer;
There humbly fall before his feet,
  For none can perish there.

[Verse 2]
Thy promise is my only plea,
  With this I venture nigh;
Thou call'st the burdened souls to thee,
  And such, O Lord, am I.

[Verse 3]
Bowed down beneath a load of sin,
  By Satan sorely pressed;
By wars without and fears within,
  I come to thee for rest.

[Verse 4]
Oh, wondrous love! to bleed and die,
  To bear the cross and shame;
That guilty sinners, such as I,
  Might plead thy gracious name.

hymns.title: Would you lose your load of sin?
hymns.author: D. W. Whittle.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Would you lose your load of sin?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Would you know God's peace within?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

Cho.--Jesus who on the cross did die,
      Jesus who lives and reigns on high,
      He alone can justify;
      Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

[Verse 2]
Would you calmly walk the wave?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Would you know his pow'r to save?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

[Verse 3]
Would you have your cares grow light?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Would you songs have in the night?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

[Verse 4]
Grieving, would you comfort know?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
Humble be when blessings flow?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

[Verse 5]
Would you strength in weakness have?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus;
See a light beyond the grave?
  Fix your eyes upon Jesus.

hymns.title: Oh, wondrous, deep, unbounded love
hymns.author: Fanny Crosby, 1873.
hymns.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Oh, wondrous, deep, unbounded love,
  My Savior, can it be
That thou hast borne the crown of thorns
  And suffered death for me?

Cho.--At the cross, at the cross, where I first saw the light
        And, the burden of my heart rolled away--
